title: Minestrone
description: My Thermomix take on a Julia Busuttil Nishimura-style minestrone — a hearty, vegetable-packed Italian soup with pasta, beans and parmesan.
keywords: Julia Busuttil Nishimura inspired Thermomix recipe
intro: This is my independent Thermomix homage to Julia Busuttil Nishimura and the comforting appeal of minestrone. It keeps the spirit of the original inspiration, but the method is written fresh for TM6 and TM7 cooks who want clear settings and a warm, achievable result.
ingredients: 100 g green beans, cut into 3 cm pieces
400 g canned cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
Extra virgin olive oil, for drizzling
steps: Place onion, carrots, celery and garlic into the mixing bowl. Chop 5 sec / speed 5. Scrape down the sides.
Add olive oil. Sauté 5 min / 120°C / speed 1.
Add canned tomatoes, zucchini, green beans, cannellini beans, potato, parmesan rind (if using) and vegetable stock. Cook 20 min / 100°C / Reverse / speed 1.
Add pasta. Cook a further 12 min / 100°C / Reverse / speed 1, or until pasta is tender. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve with fresh basil and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.
tips: The parmesan rind adds a deep savoury depth — don't skip it if you have one.
For a thicker soup, mash a ladleful of beans before adding the pasta.
This soup is even better the next day.

faq.q: Can I use dried beans instead of canned?
faq.a: Yes — soak 150 g dried cannellini beans overnight, then cook them in the soup for an extra 20 minutes before adding the pasta.
Freeze without the pasta (it goes mushy). Add fresh pasta when reheating.

faq.q: Is this the original Julia Busuttil Nishimura recipe?
faq.a: No. This is Chef Aly's independent Thermomix reinterpretation inspired by Julia Busuttil Nishimura and minestrone; it is not endorsed by or affiliated with the chef.
